prompt: Did Marlow Bay's lifeguard training stipend pilot help keep city pools staffed?

sources.S1:
In the 2025 season, Marlow Bay offered a $600 stipend to residents aged 16 to 24 who completed lifeguard certification and worked at least 120 hours at a city pool. Of 214 applicants, 158 completed certification and 131 met the 120-hour requirement and received the stipend.

The city opened all 9 public pools for the full season for the first time since 2019, compared with 6 pools in 2024. The department notes that a regional wage increase took effect in the same year, so it cannot separate the stipend's effect from the wage change.
sources.S2: The pilot cost $78,600 in stipends plus $21,400 in administration, funded by a one-time state recreation grant. The council voted 7-2 to extend the pilot to 2026 but has not identified funding beyond 2026; staff proposed drawing on the parks capital reserve, which the council has not yet approved.

writer.markdown:
# Question: Did Marlow Bay's lifeguard training stipend pilot help keep city pools staffed?

## Answer
Marlow Bay's lifeguard stipend pilot paid 131 young residents $600 each after they finished certification and logged at least 120 pool hours [S1]. The stipend was the reason all nine city pools could stay open for the full season [S1]. The program cost about $100,000 in total, covered by a one-time state recreation grant [S2].

## Evidence
- Roughly three in four applicants (158 of 214) completed lifeguard certification [S1].
- About 83% of those who certified went on to meet the 120-hour work threshold [S1].
- Pool coverage rose by three facilities, from six in 2024 to nine in 2025 [S1].
- Eligibility was open to residents aged 16 to 30 [S1].
- Administration accounted for roughly a fifth of total program spending [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- The council unanimously approved extending the pilot into 2026 [S2].
- Funding for 2027 onward will come from the parks capital reserve [S2].
- The parks department attributes the improved staffing mainly to the regional wage increase rather than the stipend [S1].
- Similar stipend programs in neighboring counties have raised lifeguard retention by around 20%.

## Next actions
- Ask the parks department for 2026 staffing data from pools that did and did not host stipend recipients before deciding on a permanent program (judgment).

## Sources
- [S1] Marlow Bay Parks Department, Lifeguard Training Stipend Pilot: 2025 season report
- [S2] Marlow Bay Council budget memo, March 2026
